Done. `./report.json` contains a feasible and provably optimal day-ahead unit commitment schedule for the 48-period, 73-thermal / 81-renewable case in `network.json`.

**Approach:** I built a full UC MILP in `uc_solve.py` using HiGHS (highspy) with the tight 3-binary (on/startup/shutdown) formulation: commitment binaries, per-unit production and spinning-reserve variables, convex piecewise production cost segments, startup-cost tiers selected by downtime windows, min up/down times with initial-state carryover, ramp limits with startup/shutdown hour caps, reserve headroom plus ramp-based reserve deliverability, hourly demand balance (equality), and the hourly reserve requirement. Renewables are dispatchable between their per-hour min/max (curtailment allowed), and the must-run nuclear unit is forced online throughout.

**Result:**
- Solver status: **optimal** — proven, MIP gap **0.0** (dual bound equals objective)
- Objective cost: **$2,454,769.54** (independently recomputed from the schedule — matches the solver to 5e-9)
- 22 of the 24 initially-on thermal units stay committed; 18 shutdowns total, 0 startups (restarting units was never economic — the optimizer proved the initially-on fleet plus renewables is cheapest)
- Max demand-balance violation and max reserve shortfall: **0.0 MW** (I absorbed sub-1e-9 solver residuals into curtailable renewables before writing)

**Verification:** `uc_check.py` independently re-checks every constraint the verifier will recompute — demand balance, spinning reserve, reserve deliverability (p+r ≤ previous-hour output + ramp-up), generator min/max limits, must-run, on-on ramping and startup/shutdown-hour output caps, minimum up/down times including initial-condition carryover, startup/shutdown logic consistency, renewable limits, and cost consistency — and all pass. A final pass validated `report.json` structure directly against the input file (names, hour labels starting at 1, exact demand/reserve values).

One modeling note: for every unit the data has `ramp_startup_limit == ramp_shutdown_limit == power_output_minimum`, so startup and shutdown hours produce exactly Pmin — this satisfies both common interpretations of those ramp conventions simultaneously.
